# AgentCom.org — full machine context

Generated from canonical structured records. Last source-verification sweep: 2026-09-08.

# Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)

Open commerce protocol for interoperable journeys between consumer surfaces, businesses, agents, and payment providers. Supports API, MCP, and A2A bindings.

**Type:** protocol

**Status:** active

**Tags:** commerce, checkout, catalog, orders, mcp, a2a

**Maintainers:** Google, Shopify and ecosystem partners

## Capabilities

- catalog discovery
- cart
- checkout
- orders
- capability negotiation

## Machine notes

- Businesses publish a profile at /.well-known/ucp.
- Shopify exposes UCP-shaped MCP tools for catalog, cart, checkout, and orders.

## Sources

- [UCP specification](https://ucp.dev/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [UCP GitHub](https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/ucp) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [Google: Under the Hood — UCP](https://developers.googleblog.com/en/under-the-hood-universal-commerce-protocol-ucp/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

## Machine alternates

- JSON: https://agentcom.org/r/ucp.json
- Markdown: https://agentcom.org/r/ucp.md
- MCP: https://agentcom.org/mcp


---

# Model Context Protocol (MCP)

Standard protocol for exposing tools, resources, and prompts to AI applications. AgentCom uses MCP as its primary agent-facing query interface.

**Type:** protocol

**Status:** active

**Tags:** tools, resources, prompts, agents

**Maintainers:** Model Context Protocol project

## Capabilities

- tools
- resources
- prompts
- streamable HTTP
- stdio

## Machine notes

- Current TypeScript SDK v2 implements the 2026-07-28 MCP specification.

## Sources

- [MCP documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [Official MCP TypeScript SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

## Machine alternates

- JSON: https://agentcom.org/r/mcp.json
- Markdown: https://agentcom.org/r/mcp.md
- MCP: https://agentcom.org/mcp

# Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP)

Open standard connecting buyers, AI agents, and businesses for product discovery and commerce interactions.

**Type:** protocol

**Status:** beta

**Tags:** commerce, openai, stripe, product-feeds, checkout

**Maintainers:** OpenAI, Stripe

## Capabilities

- product discovery
- merchant feeds
- commerce interactions

## Machine notes

- OpenAI expanded ACP to product discovery in 2026.

## Sources

- [ACP documentation](https://agenticcommerce.dev/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [ACP GitHub](https://github.com/agentic-commerce-protocol/agentic-commerce-protocol) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [OpenAI: Powering Product Discovery in ChatGPT](https://openai.com/index/powering-product-discovery-in-chatgpt/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

# Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)

Open protocol for secure, interoperable payments involving AI agents, designed to work alongside commerce and agent interoperability protocols.

**Type:** protocol

**Status:** active

**Tags:** payments, authorization, a2a, ucp

**Maintainers:** Google / FIDO ecosystem

## Capabilities

- payment authorization
- agent payment flows
- mandates

## Machine notes

- AP2 can be used as an extension alongside A2A and UCP.

## Sources

- [AP2 documentation](https://ap2-protocol.org/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [AP2 GitHub](https://github.com/google-agentic-commerce/AP2) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

## Machine alternates

- JSON: https://agentcom.org/r/ap2.json
- Markdown: https://agentcom.org/r/ap2.md
- MCP: https://agentcom.org/mcp

# Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)

Open protocol for communication and interoperability between independent agentic applications.

**Type:** protocol

**Status:** active

**Tags:** agents, interoperability, json-rpc, discovery

**Maintainers:** Linux Foundation A2A Project

## Capabilities

- agent discovery
- tasks
- streaming
- push notifications
- structured data

## Machine notes

- A2A complements MCP: A2A connects agents to agents; MCP connects agents to tools and resources.

## Sources

- [A2A documentation](https://a2a-protocol.org/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [A2A GitHub](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

## Machine alternates

- JSON: https://agentcom.org/r/a2a.json
- Markdown: https://agentcom.org/r/a2a.md
- MCP: https://agentcom.org/mcp

# x402

HTTP-native payments protocol centered on 402 Payment Required, with SDKs for machine and agent payments.

**Type:** protocol

**Status:** active

**Tags:** payments, http-402, stablecoins, machine-commerce

**Maintainers:** x402 Foundation ecosystem

## Capabilities

- pay-per-request
- payment middleware
- machine payments

## Machine notes

- Useful for paid APIs, datasets, compute, and agent-to-service transactions.

## Sources

- [x402 GitHub](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

## Machine alternates

- JSON: https://agentcom.org/r/x402.json
- Markdown: https://agentcom.org/r/x402.md
- MCP: https://agentcom.org/mcp

# Machine Payments Protocol (MPP)

Open standard for machine-to-machine payments using an HTTP payment flow, designed for agentic payments and usage-based services.

**Type:** protocol

**Status:** active

**Tags:** payments, http-402, agents, usage-based

**Maintainers:** Tempo, Stripe

## Capabilities

- inline payment negotiation
- microtransactions
- recurring payments
- machine payments

## Machine notes

- Co-authored by Tempo and Stripe; supports agents paying for services without pre-created billing accounts.

## Sources

- [MPP documentation](https://mpp.dev/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [MPP specifications](https://github.com/tempoxyz/mpp-specs) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [Stripe: Introducing MPP](https://stripe.com/blog/machine-payments-protocol) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

## Machine alternates

- JSON: https://agentcom.org/r/mpp.json
- Markdown: https://agentcom.org/r/mpp.md
- MCP: https://agentcom.org/mcp

- Cart MCP
- Checkout MCP
- Order MCP

# Make a Shopify store agent-ready

A practical checklist for Shopify merchants: agents.md, UCP discovery, catalog quality, policies, and transaction surfaces.

**Type:** guide

**Platform:** shopify

**Tags:** shopify, ucp, mcp, agents.md, agent-seo

## Steps

1. Open /agents.md on the storefront and verify it accurately describes the store and commerce capabilities.
2. Open /.well-known/ucp and record the supported UCP version, capabilities, transport, and MCP endpoint.
3. Test catalog discovery against the store MCP endpoint using an agent profile URL.
4. Verify variant-level product facts: identifiers, price, currency, availability, media, and descriptions.
5. Make shipping, returns, contact, and fulfillment policies directly accessible and unambiguous.
6. Track agent referrals and checkout handoffs separately from ordinary browser traffic.

## Sources

- [Shopify agentic commerce docs](https://shopify.dev/docs/agents) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [Shopify agents.md](https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/architecture/templates/agents-md-liquid) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [Shopify UCP/MCP discovery tutorial](https://shopify.dev/docs/agents/get-started/build-a-cart) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

## Machine alternates

- JSON: https://agentcom.org/r/shopify-agent-readiness.json
- Markdown: https://agentcom.org/r/shopify-agent-readiness.md
- MCP: https://agentcom.org/mcp

# Prepare for Google UCP / Gemini commerce

A merchant-oriented checklist for getting product data and checkout infrastructure ready for Google UCP onboarding.

**Type:** guide

**Platform:** google

**Tags:** google, merchant-center, ucp, gemini

## Steps

1. Keep Merchant Center account and product data compliant and current.
2. Implement the UCP technical requirements before expecting program onboarding.
3. Publish and validate the required UCP business profile and identity linkage.
4. Validate native checkout APIs in Google's onboarding/sandbox flow when your account receives access.
5. Model agent checkout as an extension of your merchant backend, not a separate storefront.

## Sources

- [Google UCP onboarding](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/16992327?hl=en) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [Google UCP-powered checkout](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/16837055?hl=en) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

## Machine alternates

- JSON: https://agentcom.org/r/google-ucp-onboarding.json
- Markdown: https://agentcom.org/r/google-ucp-onboarding.md
- MCP: https://agentcom.org/mcp

# Prepare products for discovery in ChatGPT

How to make merchant/product data complete, current, and suitable for ChatGPT shopping and ACP-based product discovery.

**Type:** guide

**Platform:** openai

**Tags:** openai, chatgpt, acp, product-feed, agent-seo

## Steps

1. Use stable product and variant identifiers across feeds and your storefront.
2. Keep price and availability synchronized frequently enough to avoid stale recommendations.
3. Provide specific attributes that help an agent satisfy constraints, not only marketing copy.
4. For direct-feed eligible merchants, follow OpenAI's current product feed specification and application flow.
5. For Shopify or Etsy, improve the upstream catalog because those platforms already provide product data to ChatGPT.
6. Measure assisted traffic and downstream conversion rather than only classic search rankings.

## Sources

- [OpenAI product discovery announcement](https://openai.com/index/powering-product-discovery-in-chatgpt/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [ChatGPT merchants](https://chatgpt.com/merchants/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

## Machine alternates

- JSON: https://agentcom.org/r/chatgpt-product-discovery.json
- Markdown: https://agentcom.org/r/chatgpt-product-discovery.md
- MCP: https://agentcom.org/mcp

# Agent SEO / ACO fundamentals

A platform-neutral playbook for making a merchant legible, trustworthy, and actionable to AI agents.

**Type:** guide

**Tags:** agent-seo, aco, structured-data, discoverability

## Steps

1. Expose stable, server-rendered facts: product identity, variants, price, availability, shipping, and policies.
2. Make machine entry points explicit: sitemap, structured data, llms.txt/agents.md where applicable, APIs, MCP, and protocol discovery files.
3. Use canonical identifiers consistently across website, feeds, marketplaces, and social catalogs.
4. Publish negative constraints as clearly as positive claims: exclusions, incompatibilities, delivery limitations, and return exceptions.
5. Keep mutable facts fresh and timestamped.
6. Create deterministic task paths for search, compare, cart, checkout, order lookup, returns, and support.
7. Test with agents and record failures as data-quality bugs.

## Sources

- [Stripe technical field guide](https://stripe.com/guides/how-to-prepare-for-agentic-commerce-technical-field-guide) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [llms.txt proposal](https://llmstxt.org/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

## Machine alternates

- JSON: https://agentcom.org/r/agent-seo-basics.json
- Markdown: https://agentcom.org/r/agent-seo-basics.md
- MCP: https://agentcom.org/mcp

# Expose commerce knowledge through MCP

Design an MCP server that gives agents authoritative commerce resources and narrowly-scoped tools.

**Type:** guide

**Tags:** mcp, tools, resources, commerce

## Steps

1. Expose read-only resources for policies, schemas, product definitions, and integration guidance.
2. Use tools only when the agent must compute, query fresh state, or cause an action.
3. Return structuredContent or JSON objects in addition to human-readable summaries.
4. Keep tool schemas narrow and explicit; never hide required parameters inside prose.
5. Separate public knowledge tools from authenticated merchant actions.
6. Version machine resources and include provenance.

## Sources

- [MCP documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [MCP TypeScript SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

## Machine alternates

- JSON: https://agentcom.org/r/mcp-for-commerce-resources.json
- Markdown: https://agentcom.org/r/mcp-for-commerce-resources.md
- MCP: https://agentcom.org/mcp

# Add machine payments with Stripe / MPP

When and how to make an API, dataset, compute service, or agent-accessible endpoint payable by machines.

**Type:** guide

**Platform:** stripe

**Tags:** stripe, mpp, machine-payments, api

## Steps

1. Identify a unit that is naturally payable per request, session, result, or usage block.
2. Publish clear machine-readable pricing and what the payment unlocks.
3. Use MPP-compatible payment negotiation instead of requiring a human-created billing account where appropriate.
4. Design idempotency and receipts into paid tool calls.
5. Expose testnet/sandbox examples before production money movement.

## Sources

- [MPP docs](https://mpp.dev/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [Stripe MPP announcement](https://stripe.com/blog/machine-payments-protocol) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [Stripe machine payments samples](https://github.com/stripe-samples/machine-payments) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

## Machine alternates

- JSON: https://agentcom.org/r/stripe-machine-payments.json
- Markdown: https://agentcom.org/r/stripe-machine-payments.md
- MCP: https://agentcom.org/mcp

# Build a clean TikTok Shop product data pipeline

Treat TikTok Shop as another structured commerce surface with synchronized product state and webhook-driven updates.

**Type:** guide

**Platform:** tiktok

**Tags:** tiktok, catalog, products-api, social-commerce

## Steps

1. Map your canonical SKU/variant model to TikTok Shop product records.
2. Synchronize title, description, media, pricing, inventory, and required sales terms.
3. Use create/edit APIs for controlled updates rather than manual drift.
4. Consume product webhooks to track review and state changes.
5. Record per-market differences in required product creation fields.

## Sources

- [TikTok Shop Products API](https://partner.tiktokshop.com/docv2/page/products-api-overview) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

# Create a canonical Meta Commerce catalog

A baseline for keeping Facebook and Instagram commerce product data structured, stable, and synchronized.

**Type:** guide

**Platform:** meta

**Tags:** meta, commerce-manager, catalog, product-feed

## Steps

1. Create and own the catalog in the correct Meta business account.
2. Use stable product IDs that map back to canonical SKUs/variants.
3. Choose a repeatable sync method: partner integration, data feed, or API.
4. Keep product details and availability fresh and resolve diagnostics quickly.
5. Keep return policy, shipping eligibility, and storefront data consistent with the catalog.
6. Treat the Meta catalog as a downstream projection of one canonical product source, not a manually edited database.

## Sources

- [Meta Blueprint product catalogs](https://www.facebookblueprint.com/student/path/219728) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

## Machine alternates

- JSON: https://agentcom.org/r/meta-catalog-foundation.json
- Markdown: https://agentcom.org/r/meta-catalog-foundation.md
- MCP: https://agentcom.org/mcp

# Publish commerce content for agents, not just browsers

A content architecture for publishing the same authoritative fact as HTML, Markdown, JSON, feeds, and protocol resources.

**Type:** guide

**Tags:** machine-readable, json, markdown, llms.txt, api

## Steps

1. Store content as structured records with provenance and verification dates.
2. Render human HTML from those records instead of duplicating facts in templates.
3. Offer JSON and Markdown alternates at predictable URLs.
4. Publish llms.txt as an index, not as a replacement for canonical source records.
5. Provide a searchable API and NDJSON bulk export.
6. Expose the same graph through MCP resources/tools.
7. Use source freshness rules so stale instructions can be flagged automatically.

## Sources

- [llms.txt proposal](https://llmstxt.org/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [MCP documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

## Machine alternates

- JSON: https://agentcom.org/r/machine-readable-commerce-content.json
- Markdown: https://agentcom.org/r/machine-readable-commerce-content.md
- MCP: https://agentcom.org/mcp

# Choose the right agentic-commerce protocol

A practical map: use MCP for tools/resources, A2A for agent collaboration, UCP/ACP for commerce flows, and AP2/x402/MPP for payments depending on the use case.

**Type:** guide

**Tags:** ucp, acp, mcp, a2a, ap2, x402, mpp

## Steps

1. Need an agent to use your tools or read authoritative resources? Start with MCP.
2. Need independent agents to discover and collaborate with each other? Evaluate A2A.
3. Need merchant discovery/cart/checkout/order interoperability? Evaluate UCP and the commerce surfaces your target platforms actually support.
4. Need OpenAI-specific merchant/product discovery integration? Track ACP and OpenAI merchant feed requirements.
5. Need authorized agent payments? Evaluate AP2 in the relevant commerce flow.
6. Need machine-pay-per-request economics? Evaluate x402 or MPP.
7. Do not implement every protocol by default; implement the smallest set that maps to an active distribution channel.

## Sources

- [UCP](https://ucp.dev/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [ACP](https://agenticcommerce.dev/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [A2A](https://a2a-protocol.org/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [AP2](https://ap2-protocol.org/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [x402](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402) — primary; verified 2026-09-08
- [MPP](https://mpp.dev/) — primary; verified 2026-09-08

## Machine alternates

- JSON: https://agentcom.org/r/protocol-selection-map.json
- Markdown: https://agentcom.org/r/protocol-selection-map.md
- MCP: https://agentcom.org/mcp
